title: Guarded atomic task execution with durable intent and conservative resume
request: Implement the next task-planning package with only affected tests, then continue to TP-05 after finishing and committing TP-04 as the owner subsequently requested.
plan: Map the existing solution team, project stores, registry guards, stage lineage, holdout receipt and checkpoint saver.
Write failing real-stage and readiness tests, then integrate one explicit task path into the existing solution team.
Save intent in the existing saver before a registry effect; serialize project effects and reconcile actual owner evidence without guessing.
Exercise file and PostgreSQL crash, permission, source, privacy, budget and stop boundaries on invented data.
Fix independent review findings, run selected compatibility checks, record acceptance and rebuild the development corpus.

decisions.decision: Use the existing SolutionTeam and its saver, with a separate task checkpoint namespace.
decisions.why: The team already owns stage order, audits and human pauses. A saver namespace keeps durable pre-effect attempts without another graph, database or stale project-document overwrite.

decisions.decision: Use separate solution-invocation and project-effect locks, implemented by the file and PostgreSQL stores.
decisions.why: Graph nodes can run on another thread. Reusing a parent thread's effect lock could deadlock, while concurrent dispatchers must not claim the same effect.

decisions.decision: Associate a stage with its attempt through the existing nonsemantic lineage parent.
decisions.why: Putting an attempt identifier into scientific input references would change faithful replay fingerprints. Parent provenance preserves the relationship without changing those inputs.

decisions.decision: Reconcile exact completed owner records; leave intent-only or partial owner commits blocked.
decisions.why: A tool reply or stage status is not sufficient evidence after a crash. Matching records, current inputs, upstream runs and holdout receipts prevent duplicate effects or extra final scoring.

decisions.decision: Keep operation completion distinct from scientific acceptance.
decisions.why: The existing adapter documents missing fold, threshold and report proof. Task attempts explicitly leave acceptance pending for TP-05 rather than inferring that every criterion passed.

decisions.decision: Run the first explicit task path without model calls and keep product defaults unchanged.
decisions.why: This slice validates existing deterministic tools and crash boundaries. It adds no unmeasured live model spend, public route or rollout.

decisions.decision: Rebuild source decisions from the authenticated project and retain only their immutable hashes in task checkpoints.
decisions.why: Confirmed source decisions can still contain private class values. Their bodies are unnecessary for safe current-source validation and should not be copied into task records.

change: Add an explicit task mode to the existing solution team and a small one-action dispatcher. Reuse frozen core plans and the guarded registry/engine, store pre-effect intent in the existing saver, add workspace-scoped process locks, preserve actual owner evidence and budget history, and block unknown effects without replay. No independent acceptance verifier or selective replan is introduced.

findings.defect: Advisory session locks occupied a pooled data connection while the owner needed another connection to save.
findings.scenario: With a one-connection pool and no overflow, a project turn followed by a project read timed out; waiting lock callers could also starve the owner.
findings.cause: The long-lived lock session was checked out from the same finite pool as ordinary data transactions.
findings.fix: Detach the advisory connection before waiting and close the detached session after unlocking, preserving driver settings while freeing the data pool slot.
findings.test: The reviewer independently reproduced the original timeout. The single-slot PostgreSQL regression checks owner reads/writes, a waiting caller and same-thread store-instance reentrancy.
findings.impact: A supported small pool could deadlock or reject project writes despite no competing scientific work.

findings.defect: Reading a checkpoint by bare project identifier could expose another workspace's task state.
findings.scenario: A dispatcher bound to another workspace requested the known project identifier through the shared PostgreSQL checkpoint tables.
findings.cause: The saver has no project ownership boundary, and the initial state reader did not call the project store first.
findings.fix: Authenticate ownership through Projects.get before saver reads and before a solution invocation can return a paused question.
findings.test: A second PostgreSQL workspace cannot read task state or invoke the other project's paused team, while the original workspace still resumes normally.
findings.impact: Project metadata and task plans could cross the workspace boundary.

findings.defect: A known duration overrun disappeared when completion was reconciled after a crash.
findings.scenario: An owner stage took longer than its reserved plan limit and finished, but the terminal task checkpoint was interrupted; resume initially allowed the next stage.
findings.cause: Normal return compared elapsed time with the limit, while reconciliation bypassed that comparison.
findings.fix: Return the owner's duration as evidence, conservatively retain at least the reservation and preserve the overrun flag during reconciliation.
findings.test: A reviewer probe reproduced the original overrun loss. The regression injects an authored over-limit owner duration after an interrupted terminal checkpoint and requires the next action to stop.
findings.impact: Repeated resumes could exceed a known execution-time allowance.

findings.defect: The legacy file store's thread-only fallback could not guarantee cross-process task exclusivity on unsupported platforms.
findings.scenario: A platform without the POSIX file-lock facility enabled the new task dispatcher.
findings.cause: The inherited lock helper intentionally allowed a legacy thread-only fallback.
findings.fix: Require process locking explicitly for task execution and task-enabled team invocation while preserving the old fallback for legacy file operations.
findings.test: The file-only regression removes the process-lock facility and requires refusal before a checkpoint or effect. Kernel probes verify both same-ID workspace locks remain held.
findings.impact: Two processes could otherwise dispatch the same task on an unsupported file platform.

findings.defect: The initial checkpoint copied full source decisions, including a potentially private positive-class label.
findings.scenario: An invented binary table uses a unique private-marker class value and the owner confirms it as the positive label; the marker initially appears in task state.
findings.cause: Keeping the complete source plan duplicated a value that was unnecessary for task validation.
findings.fix: Keep the graph's source hashes only, rebuild source contracts from the authenticated current project, and compare their current immutable identities before effects.
findings.test: The new private-class checkpoint test failed before the fix, then passed on file and PostgreSQL storage. Current-source and full-chain regressions also passed afterward.
findings.impact: A sensitive target category could have been unnecessarily copied into a task checkpoint.

findings.defect: A measurement-limit sentence introduced a package identifier that the corpus numeric-grounding gate interpreted as an unsupported number.
findings.scenario: The development corpus rejected one judgment example although its test counts were grounded, because a later-package label appeared only in its answer limits.
findings.cause: The evidence-reading gate parses the numeric suffix of a package label as a number, and the measurement prompt did not include that suffix.
findings.fix: Describe the next package in words inside the measurement limits; keep its explicit identifier in the surrounding development record.
findings.test: Rebuild the corpus and run the four development-record and freshness tests without changing or weakening the numeric-grounding gate.
findings.impact: The completion corpus would remain partially refused and fail its required freshness checks.

measurements.name: Test-first effect and readiness boundary
measurements.gate: The real-stage/no-repeat and unready-task tests fail before a dispatcher exists, then pass after implementation.
measurements.result: The initial module import failed because the dispatcher did not exist; the implemented real stage and readiness boundary then passed.

measurements.name: Relevant execution and compatibility checks
measurements.gate: All selected dispatch, storage/lock, holdout and affected existing workflow/lineage/harness checks pass without live or sealed evaluations.
measurements.result: 74 distinct relevant checks passed: 46 dispatcher tests, six storage-interface/lock tests, six holdout crash-safety tests and 16 selected compatibility tests. The dispatcher group includes 22 file and 24 PostgreSQL cases. No skips.
limits: No full repository, full PostgreSQL suite or broad product-flow gate ran.
The seeded invented Telco-shaped fixture measures execution invariants, not real-user performance or production readiness.
Scientific acceptance is pending for the next package; owner-operation completion is narrower.

measurements.name: Independent adversarial review
measurements.gate: Every confirmed correctness finding is fixed and the final reviewed implementation has no remaining correctness finding.
measurements.result: Review passed after pool, ownership, recovered-time and unsupported-process-lock fixes. The reviewer independently reproduced the pool and duration failures before their fixes.
limits: A final self-found source-payload privacy issue was additionally fixed and verified by failing-before/passing-after tests on both backends.

outcome: TP-04 complete under the owner's affected-test scope. Existing guarded tools execute one task at a time with durable attempts, safe owner-evidence reconciliation and conservative stops. The owner authorized TP-05 after this commit; no TP-05 implementation is included here.
lessons: Checkpoint persistence does not make an external side effect atomic; durable intent and exact owner evidence are still required.
An advisory-lock waiter must not consume the finite connection pool that its owner needs.
A shared saver is a persistence mechanism, not project authorization.
Recovery must preserve budget overruns as carefully as normal return.
Confirmed source decisions can contain private class values; source hashes are enough for task checkpoints.
Distinguish owner-operation completion from independent scientific acceptance.
risks: Unknown effects and incomplete owner metadata remain blocked until their existing owner reconciles them.
The first task path supports fresh basic binary projects and requires reliable process locking.
Time budgets are checked at task boundaries and do not hard-cancel an in-flight scientific computation.
Independent acceptance, selective invalidation and bounded recovery policy remain TP-05 work.
